review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read RationalHeight.lean (RationalHeightLE, mono), DilationPairCoordinates.lean (scaledPairLayer, scaledPairLayerEquiv, scaledPairAssemble) and the single call site in ControlledComparisonModel.lean (line 128). The theorem is tied to ℚ throughout. The scalar q : ℚ, the ℚ-submodules and RationalHeightLE (numerator and denominator) are all rational-specific, so no useful field-level generalisation exists. Separate height bounds for a and b would give a max bound with no consumer, because the only caller uses the same H for both. Replacing Fintype by Finite is cosmetic. The hypotheses hH and hK can be recovered from other hypotheses (a denominator is at least 1), but removing a binder belongs to the separate unnecessary-hypotheses experiment, so I did not report it. I found no justified finding under this rubric.
